newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 97/98 crop financing over 8 bln reais-AgMin.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 97/98 crop financing over 8 bln reais-AgMin.

text.p: Brazil will allocate a minimum of eight billion reais ($7.5 billion) to subsidize agriculture in 1997/98, up from 5.2 billion the previous year, the Agriculture Ministry said.
"The minister told sector officials the safest thing was to work with (a level of) more than eight billion," a spokeswoman at the ministry said.
Subsidies could reach a maximum of 10 billion reais, Agriculture Minister Arlindo Porto reportedly told sector officials at a meeting to discuss the new crop plan.
Porto announced the range and said the definitive figure should be announced Wednesday, according to a spokesman for the National Confederation of Agriculture (CNA) who was present at the meeting.
The meeting also heard a proposal to raise the financing limit for soybeans to 90,000 reais per farmer from 30,000 reais, the CNA official said.
"It still hasn't been decided, but with this financing increase there would be a stimulus to production of a commodity that has a strong market abroad," he said.
Other commodities eligible for financing -- mostly basic products including rice, beans, corn and wheat -- currently benefit from a limit of 150,000 reais per farmer, he said.
"The soybean sector has been receiving less because it has the best structure and is considered a sector which can obtain financing from other sources," the spokesman said.
But some government technicians were lobbying for greater investment in the soybean crop, which together with coffee is a key export revenue earner for Brazil.
Brazil posted a $271 million trade deficit in May, its lowest shortfall in 12 months thanks to seasonal hikes in agricultural exports.

World coffee prices have soared this year amid tight demand, while Brazil's 1996/97 soybean harvest is on track to becoming the largest on record after continued high international prices encouraged farmers to plant a bigger crop.
